definition: EV sales as a share of total sales in a segment, for example e-2W units divided by all 2W units. This is the main measure of how far the transition has progressed.

The two dominant lithium-ion cell chemistries. LFP (lithium iron phosphate) is cheaper, safer and longer-lasting but less energy-dense. NMC (nickel manganese cobalt) offers more range per kg at a higher cost and with more commodity exposure.
Battery pack cost per kilowatt-hour of capacity. Because the pack is the largest cost in an EV, this figure drives price parity with ICE vehicles.

Production Linked Incentive schemes that reward incremental domestic sales of Advanced Chemistry Cells and of advanced automotive technology. Eligibility depends on localisation and investment thresholds.
India's demand-incentive scheme for e-2W, e-3W, e-buses, e-trucks and charging infrastructure, which succeeded FAME-II.
MoRTH's national vehicle registration database. It is the standard source for monthly EV registration data in India.

Retail is registrations to end customers (FADA and Vahan). Wholesale is factory dispatches to dealers (SIAM and company data). The gap between the two shows whether channel inventory is building or being drawn down.
Dealer stock expressed as days of sales. Elevated levels point to discounting and future production cuts.
Average revenue per vehicle sold, driven by mix (SUVs, premium models), pricing and exports.
The split of sales across petrol, diesel, CNG, hybrid and EV. It matters for supplier exposure and capex allocation.
The 2025 rationalisation of GST rates that lowered taxes on many vehicle categories. Buyers deferred purchases ahead of it, which distorts year-on-year comparisons for September 2025.
New contracts won in a period, and the total unexecuted backlog. Order book divided by trailing revenue gives years of revenue visibility.
Order inflow divided by revenue. A ratio above 1.0x means the backlog is growing.
A contract term that passes commodity cost changes on to the customer. Fixed-price contracts without a PVC expose margins to steel, copper and aluminium price swings.
Engineering, Procurement and Construction: turnkey project contracting. Margins are thin and working capital is heavy, so execution risk sits with the contractor.
Receivable days plus inventory days minus payable days. This is a key cash-conversion metric for capital goods and EPC companies.
Power transmission and distribution: transformers, switchgear, cables, substations and HVDC links.
Defence Acquisition Procedure 2020, the rulebook for capital procurement by the Indian armed forces. It defines the buy categories and their indigenous-content requirements.
The highest-priority DAP category, for products that are Indigenously Designed, Developed and Manufactured. It typically requires at least 50% indigenous content.
MoD lists of items that can no longer be imported after specified dates, which creates a guaranteed domestic market for local suppliers.
Obligations on foreign OEMs to reinvest part of a contract's value in Indian industry, historically a route to aerostructure and component work.
Firm orders not yet delivered. Airbus and Boeing backlogs of several years support supplier visibility.
Spares, maintenance, repair and overhaul revenue. It typically carries higher margins and more recurring income than original-equipment sales.
Long-Term Agreement between an aero OEM and a supplier that sets volume shares and pricing for a programme, often over 5–10 years.
Offer for Sale: existing shareholders sell shares in an IPO or follow-on, so the proceeds go to the sellers rather than the company.
Qualified Institutional Placement: a fast-track equity raise by a listed Indian company from qualified institutional buyers.
A split of a company's businesses into separate entities, with shareholders receiving shares in the new entity. Shareholders on the record date are entitled to the new shares.
Enterprise value divided by EBITDA. It is the default trading and transaction multiple for industrials because it is capital-structure neutral.
A valuation method that applies multiples paid in comparable past M&A deals. These multiples usually include a control premium.
The excess over the unaffected share price that an acquirer pays for control, often 20–40% in public M&A.
